findings.text: vesselExport ignores input.id and always returns { vessel: 'anonymous' }. Corpus rule T-1 requires the caller's vessel id to be preserved verbatim in the vessel field, so A1 is unmet and obligation I-1 does not hold.

findings.text: The only test asserts typeof vessel === 'string'. It passes with the hard-coded 'anonymous' return, so the green unit lane and the satisfied witness-presence check do not show that T-1 behaviour ran. The test must assert the supplied id comes back verbatim.

experiments.output: tests 1, pass 1, fail 0 (against the implementation that returns 'anonymous' for every id)

directives: Change vesselExport in packages/flint/src/vessel-export.ts to return { vessel: input.id }, unchanged (no trimming, casing or defaulting), so it satisfies T-1. Do not log the token or write it anywhere (T-2).

Replace the typeof-only check in packages/flint/test/vessel-export.test.ts with assertions that vessel strictly equals the supplied id, using at least two distinct ids and one with characters a normaliser would alter, such as 'MV-42 '. The test must fail against a constant return. Keep the test name that the 'export' witness selects, or make sure the witness still selects this test.
Rerun node tools/gen-goldens.ts after the fix and commit its output only. Do not hand-edit goldens or change anything else.
reasons: A1: NOT MET. The function and test exist and accept an id and token, but the record does not follow the export contract: T-1 is violated because the id is discarded for the constant 'anonymous'. T-2 is not violated; the token is unused and nothing is logged.

A2: MET at this head. The executor's regeneration was byte-identical, and a parsed comparison of goldens/flint.json against the baseline shows only the new vessel-export.ts module entry and no removals. The diff touches no other files. Goldens must be regenerated again if the fix changes the signature or imported calls.
I-1 (anchored at T-1) does not hold. The green unit lane and witness presence are not evidence for it because the test cannot detect the violation.

premises.claim: T-1 requires the vessel field to carry the caller-supplied id verbatim.
The implementation returns a constant and never reads input.id.
The test checks only the type of the vessel field.
